claim: Recent research suggests that in central mammalian synapses, active zones contain several docking sites acting in parallel.
source: Recent research suggests that in central mammalian synapses, active zones contain several docking sites acting in parallel.
evidence: This is a general statement about current understanding in the field, supported by the broader scientific literature.

claim: Before release, one or several synaptic vesicles (SVs) are thought to bind to each docking site, forming the readily releasable pool (RRP).
source: Before release, one or several synaptic vesicles (SVs) are thought to bind to each docking site, forming the readily releasable pool (RRP).
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific understanding about SV binding and RRP formation.

claim: Determining the RRP size per docking site has important implications for short-term synaptic plasticity.
source: Determining the RRP size per docking site has important implications for short-term synaptic plasticity.
evidence: This is a reasoning statement about the significance of the research question.

claim: Under conditions maximizing release probability, occupancy of docking sites, and synaptic depression, the RRP size reached a maximum value close to two SVs per docking site.
source: Under these conditions, the RRP size reached a maximum value close to two SVs per docking site.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental measurements.

claim: Each docking site contains two distinct SV-binding sites that can simultaneously accommodate up to one SV each.
source: The results indicate that each docking site contains two distinct SV-binding sites that can simultaneously accommodate up to one SV each.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data regarding the structure of docking sites.

claim: Under special experimental conditions, as both sites are close to full occupancy, a maximal RRP size of two SVs per docking site can be reached.
source: They further suggest that under special experimental conditions, as both sites are close to full occupancy, a maximal RRP size of two SVs per docking site can be reached.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data under specific conditions.

claim: The results validate a sequential two-step docking model previously proposed at this preparation.
source: More generally, the results validate a sequential two-step docking model previously proposed at this preparation.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the consistency of the data with a previously proposed model.

claim: Functional studies using variance/mean analysis of synaptic currents indicate that within individual AZs, exocytosis occurs at a finite number of structures called docking or release sites.
source: Functional studies using variance/mean analysis of synaptic currents (Clements and Silver, 2000) or direct visualization of SV fusion (Maschi and Klyachko, 2017; Sakamoto et al., 2018) indicate that within individual AZs, exocytosis occurs at a finite number of structures called docking or release sites.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous functional studies.

claim: The number of docking sites per AZ has been estimated in a wide range of preparations, with results varying over a range of 1–15.
source: The number of docking sites per AZ has been estimated in a wide range of preparations, with results varying over a range of 1–15 (Malagon et al., 2016; Maschi and Klyachko, 2017; Neher and Sakaba, 2008; Pulido et al., 2015; Sakamoto et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: Each docking site has been proposed to be associated with a cluster of RIM 1/2.
source: Morphologically, each docking site has been proposed to be associated with a cluster of RIM 1/2 (Tang et al., 2016), voltage-gated calcium channels (Miki et al., 2017), and/or Unc 13/Munc13 (Reddy-Alla et al., 2017; Sakamoto et al., 2018).
evidence: This is based on morphological studies cited in the text.

claim: Each docking site has been proposed to be associated with voltage-gated calcium channels.
source: Morphologically, each docking site has been proposed to be associated with a cluster of RIM 1/2 (Tang et al., 2016), voltage-gated calcium channels (Miki et al., 2017), and/or Unc 13/Munc13 (Reddy-Alla et al., 2017; Sakamoto et al., 2018).
evidence: This is based on morphological studies cited in the text.

claim: Each docking site has been proposed to be associated with Unc 13/Munc13.
source: Morphologically, each docking site has been proposed to be associated with a cluster of RIM 1/2 (Tang et al., 2016), voltage-gated calcium channels (Miki et al., 2017), and/or Unc 13/Munc13 (Reddy-Alla et al., 2017; Sakamoto et al., 2018).
evidence: This is based on morphological studies cited in the text.

claim: Several clusters of the relevant protein occur inside one AZ.
source: In each case, several clusters of the relevant protein occur inside one AZ.
evidence: This is a statement about the spatial organization of proteins within active zones.

claim: It is widely accepted that exhaustion of the RRP is a main mechanism underlying synaptic depression during high-frequency neuronal activity.
source: It is widely accepted that exhaustion of the RRP is a main mechanism underlying synaptic depression during high-frequency neuronal activity (Betz, 1970; Elmqvist and Quastel, 1965; Schneggenburger et al., 1999; Thanawala and Regehr, 2013; review: Zucker and Regehr, 2002).
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus supported by multiple citations.

claim: The size of the RRP is likely related to the number of docking sites.
source: While the size of the RRP is likely related to the number of docking sites, the exact relation between the two quantities has remained unclear.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the relationship between RRP size and docking sites.

claim: The exact relation between RRP size and the number of docking sites has remained unclear.
source: While the size of the RRP is likely related to the number of docking sites, the exact relation between the two quantities has remained unclear.
evidence: This identifies a gap in current knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Under electron microscopy, filaments with various angles and lengths can be seen linking SVs to the AZ membrane.
source: Under electron microscopy, filaments with various angles and lengths can be seen linking SVs to the AZ membrane (review: Silva et al., 2021).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations cited in a review.

claim: The number and spatial arrangement of docked SV around individual docking sites is unknown.
source: Nonetheless, the number and spatial arrangement of docked SV around individual docking sites is unknown.
evidence: This identifies a limitation in current knowledge.

claim: Recently developed models assuming sequential steps of SV binding to individual docking sites have provided an explanation for a range of synaptic changes at several types of central synapses.
source: Recently developed models assuming sequential steps of SV binding to individual docking sites have provided an explanation for a range of synaptic changes at several types of central synapses (Doussau et al., 2017; Eshra et al., 2021; Fukaya et al., 2023; Kobbersmed et al., 2020; Lin et al., 2022; Miki et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent modeling studies.

claim: The basis for sequential models came from functional and modeling studies at parallel fiber to molecular layer interneuron (PF–MLI) synapses and at the calyx of Held indicating calcium-dependent docking within 5 ms after an AP stimulation.
source: The basis for these models came from functional and modeling studies at parallel fiber to molecular layer interneuron (PF–MLI) synapses and at the calyx of Held indicating calcium-dependent docking within 5 ms after an AP stimulation (Lin et al., 2022; Miki et al., 2018; Miki et al., 2016; Taschenberger et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on functional and modeling studies cited in the text.

claim: Rapid freezing electron microscopy studies in cultured hippocampal neurons show that, following an AP stimulation, SVs move rapidly (within 10 ms) to the AZ membrane in a calcium-dependent process.
source: Likewise, rapid freezing electron microscopy studies in cultured hippocampal neurons show that, following an AP stimulation, SVs move rapidly (within 10 ms) to the AZ membrane in a calcium-dependent process (Chang et al., 2018; Kusick et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy studies cited in the text.

claim: The RRP comprises two classes of SVs representing the last two steps of preparation before release.
source: These results suggest that the RRP comprises two classes of SVs representing the last two steps of preparation before release.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the cited studies.

claim: One variant of sequential models assumes that a docking site can accommodate only one SV of either class ('loose state/tight state [LS/TS] model').
source: One variant of sequential models assumes that a docking site can accommodate only one SV of either class ('loose state/tight state [LS/TS] model': Neher and Brose, 2018), while another variant assumes that a docking site can simultaneously accept two SVs, one of each class ('replacement site/docking site [RS/DS] model': Miki et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes a specific model variant with citation.

claim: Another variant of sequential models assumes that a docking site can simultaneously accept two SVs, one of each class ('replacement site/docking site [RS/DS] model').
source: One variant of sequential models assumes that a docking site can accommodate only one SV of either class ('loose state/tight state [LS/TS] model': Neher and Brose, 2018), while another variant assumes that a docking site can simultaneously accept two SVs, one of each class ('replacement site/docking site [RS/DS] model': Miki et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes another model variant with citation.

claim: A method has been developed allowing counting of SV release events at single PF–MLI synapses reliably and with an excellent time resolution.
source: We recently developed a method allowing us to count SV release events at single PF–MLI synapses reliably and with an excellent time resolution (Malagon et al., 2016).
evidence: This refers to a previously developed method by the authors.

claim: By adjusting experimental conditions to increase docking site occupancy, release probability, and docking rate, a ratio between RRP size and docking site number close to 2 was found.
source: By adjusting experimental conditions, we increase docking site occupancy, release probability, and docking rate. Under these conditions, we find a ratio between RRP size and docking site number close to 2, thus strongly constraining docking site models at this synapse.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: The RS/DS model predicts a maximum RRP size of two SVs per docking site.
source: Thus, the RS/DS model predicts a maximum RRP size per docking site of 2, whereas the LS/TS model predicts a maximum RRP size per docking site of 1.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction derived from the RS/DS model structure.

claim: The LS/TS model predicts a maximum RRP size of one SV per docking site.
source: Thus, the RS/DS model predicts a maximum RRP size per docking site of 2, whereas the LS/TS model predicts a maximum RRP size per docking site of 1.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction derived from the LS/TS model structure.

claim: In the RS/DS model, incoming SVs first bind to a distal 'replacement site', then to an associated proximal 'docking site' before being released.
source: Incoming SVs first bind to a distal 'replacement site' (upper position in Figure 1A), then to an associated proximal 'docking site' (lower position in Figure 1A) before being released.
evidence: This describes the sequential binding process in the RS/DS model, illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The distal replacement site is considered to be ~40 nm away from the plasma membrane.
source: The distal replacement site is considered to be ~40 nm away from the plasma membrane, allowing simultaneous occupancy of both distal and proximal docking sites by SVs.
evidence: This is a specific distance parameter of the RS/DS model.

claim: The distance of the replacement site from the plasma membrane allows simultaneous occupancy of both distal and proximal docking sites by SVs.
source: The distal replacement site is considered to be ~40 nm away from the plasma membrane, allowing simultaneous occupancy of both distal and proximal docking sites by SVs.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the spatial arrangement in the model.

claim: Calcium elevation in presynaptic terminals promotes the replenishment of SVs to emptied docking sites.
source: Calcium elevation in presynaptic terminals promotes the replenishment of SVs to emptied docking sites (Chang et al., 2018; Kobbersmed et al., 2020; Kusick et al., 2020; Neher and Sakaba, 2008; Sakaba, 2008; Wang and Kaczmarek, 1998; Wu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Calcium increases not only pr, but also r and s.
source: Accordingly, we assume that calcium increases not only pr, but also r and s.
evidence: This is an assumption based on the known effects of calcium on SV dynamics.

claim: As the probability of transition r increases after an AP, SVs can move from the distal to proximal site within a few ms.
source: As the probability of transition r increases after an AP, SVs can move from the distal to proximal site within a few ms.
evidence: This is a consequence of the model dynamics under calcium elevation.

claim: In the framework of the RS/DS model, both replacement and docked SVs are regarded as belonging to the RRP.
source: In the framework of the RS/DS model, due to the high speed of this transition, both replacement and docked SVs are regarded as belonging to the RRP (Miki et al., 2018; Miki et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a defining feature of the RS/DS model with citations.

claim: In the LS/TS model, the RRP comprises the sum of SVs occupying a distal and a proximal SV-binding site, which are called the loosely and tightly docked state.
source: Likewise, in the related LS/TS model, the RRP comprises the sum of SVs occupying a distal and a proximal SV-binding site, which are called in this model the loosely and tightly docked state (Lin et al., 2022; Neher and Brose, 2018; Neher and Taschenberger, 2021).
evidence: This describes the RRP composition in the LS/TS model with citations.

claim: A key difference between the RS/DS and LS/TS models is that the sites in the RS/DS model can be simultaneously occupied while in the LS/TS model a docking site can only accommodate one SV in either state at a time.
source: A key difference between these two models is that the sites in the RS/DS model can be simultaneously occupied while in the LS/TS model a docking site can only accommodate one SV in either state at a time.
evidence: This is a comparison of the structural assumptions of the two models.

claim: At PF-MLI synapses, it is possible to count the release of individual SVs with an effective time separation of 0.2 ms between consecutive release events.
source: At these synapses, it is possible to count the release of individual SVs with an effective time separation of 0.2 ms between consecutive release events (Malagon et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes a technical capability of the recording method with citation.

claim: At PF-MLI synapses, it is possible to count the number of docking sites precisely.
source: It is also possible to count the number of docking sites precisely, giving an opportunity to evaluate the maximum number of released SVs per site.
evidence: This describes another technical capability of the method.

claim: In the extreme case where pr and r are both equal to 1, a first AP should release all SVs that were initially in the docking site, and a second AP should release all SVs that were initially in the replacement site.
source: In the extreme case where pr and r are both equal to 1, a first AP should release all SVs that were initially in the docking site, and a second AP should release all SVs that were initially in the replacement site (Figure 1B; Tran et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction of the model under specific conditions, illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Under conditions where pr and r are both equal to 1, the RRP size is given by the sum of the number of released SVs for the first two APs.
source: The RRP size is then given by the sum of the number of released SVs for the two APs.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the model predictions under specific conditions.

claim: Recordings were initiated in an elevated external calcium concentration (3 mM), a condition that has been shown to elevate δ, pr, and r.
source: Recordings from simple synapses between cerebellar GCs and MLIs (Figure 1C) were initiated in an elevated external calcium concentration (3 mM), a condition that has been shown to elevate δ, pr, and r (Miki et al., 2018; Malagon et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes an experimental condition with citations supporting its effects.

claim: The potassium channel blocker 4-amidopyridine (4-AP) increases pr.
source: we applied the potassium channel blocker 4-amidopyridine (4-AP), which increases pr
evidence: This describes the effect of 4-AP on release probability.

claim: A post-tetanic potentiation (PTP) protocol results in an increase in docking site occupancy lasting several minutes.
source: This protocol (called 'PTP'hereafter) results in an increase in docking site occupancy lasting several minutes (Tran et al., 2023).
evidence: This describes the effect of the PTP protocol with citation.

claim: Group results indicate a marked enhancement in the mean released SV numbers after the first two stimuli when comparing results in 4-AP or after PTP with control.
source: Group results indicate a marked enhancement in the mean released SV numbers after the first two stimuli, and somewhat reduced responses for stimuli 5–8, when comparing results in 4-AP or after PTP with control (n = 8; Figure 2B, C showing the number of SVs released per AZ and per docking site, respectively).
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results shown in Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: The number of released SVs following stimulus number i (si) is the product of the number of docking sites (N) and the release probability at each docking site (Pi).
source: Following stimulus number i, the number of released SVs, si (Figure 2B), is the product of the number of docking sites, N, and of the release probability at each docking site, Pi (see SV release normalized to N, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a mathematical relationship used in the analysis.

claim: Variance-mean analysis and binomial analysis give the same estimate for N.
source: Therefore, the two methods give the same estimate for N (N = 4 in the present case).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing two analytical methods, shown in Figure 3A.

claim: N values did not change when adding 4-AP or after PTP induction.
source: Across experiments, N values returned by variance–mean curves did not change when adding 4-AP or after PTP induction (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The invariable N values indicate that the addition of 4-AP and the PTP protocol do not increase the number of docking sites in the time frame of the experiments.
source: The invariable N values indicate that the addition of 4-AP and the PTP protocol do not increase the number of docking sites in the time frame of the experiments.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental finding about N values.

claim: N values determined with the binomial method in 4-AP varied among experiments from 2 to 6, with a mean value of 3.6 ± 0.3 (n = 14 experiments).
source: N values determined with the binomial method in 4-AP varied among experiments from 2 to 6, with a mean value of 3.6 ± 0.3 (n = 14 experiments).
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of experimental measurements.

claim: P1 significantly increased in 4-AP compared to control (control: 0.39 ± 0.04; 4-AP: 0.69 ± 0.03, paired t-test ppt < 0.01).
source: P1 significantly increased in 4-AP compared to control, and after PTP compared to the previous data in 4-AP (control: 0.39 ± 0.04; 4-AP: 0.69 ± 0.03, paired t-test ppt < 0.01 compared to control; PTP: 0.88 ± 0.04, ppt < 0.01 compared to 4-AP; n = 14 for control and 4-AP, n = 8 for comparison after and before PTP protocol; ppt calculated for paired results; Figure 4, left).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: P1 significantly increased after PTP compared to 4-AP (4-AP: 0.69 ± 0.03; PTP: 0.88 ± 0.04, ppt < 0.01).
source: P1 significantly increased in 4-AP compared to control, and after PTP compared to the previous data in 4-AP (control: 0.39 ± 0.04; 4-AP: 0.69 ± 0.03, paired t-test ppt < 0.01 compared to control; PTP: 0.88 ± 0.04, ppt < 0.01 compared to 4-AP; n = 14 for control and 4-AP, n = 8 for comparison after and before PTP protocol; ppt calculated for paired results; Figure 4, left).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: P2 significantly increased in 4-AP compared to control (control: 0.46 ± 0.04; 4-AP: 0.64 ± 0.03, ppt < 0.01).
source: P2 significantly increased in 4-AP compared to control, and it remained stable after PTP (control: 0.46 ± 0.04; 4-AP: 0.64 ± 0.03, ppt < 0.01 compared to control; PTP: 0.67 ± 0.07, ppt > 0.05 compared to before protocol; Figure 4, middle).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: P2 remained stable after PTP compared to 4-AP (4-AP: 0.64 ± 0.03; PTP: 0.67 ± 0.07, ppt > 0.05).
source: P2 significantly increased in 4-AP compared to control, and it remained stable after PTP (control: 0.46 ± 0.04; 4-AP: 0.64 ± 0.03, ppt < 0.01 compared to control; PTP: 0.67 ± 0.07, ppt > 0.05 compared to before protocol; Figure 4, middle).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Since P1 is 0.69 in 4-AP, and 0.88 in PTP, both δ (docking site occupancy) and pr (release probability) are ≥0.69 in 4-AP, and ≥0.88 in PTP.
source: Since P1 is 0.69 in 4-AP, and 0.88 in PTP, both δ1 (noted as δ) and pr are ≥0.69 in 4-AP, and ≥0.88 in PTP.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the relation Pi = δipr and the measured P1 values.

claim: The experimental conditions reached high release probability and docking site occupancy required for a meaningful evaluation of RRP size.
source: These results indicate that we did reach the conditions of elevated release probability and docking site occupancy that are required for a meaningful evaluation of RRP size.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the experimental conditions based on the measured values.

claim: During PTP, virtually all SVs initially bound to the proximal docking site are released by the first AP.
source: During PTP, virtually all SVs initially bound to the proximal docking site are released by the first AP, making replenishment of this site necessary for release in response to the second AP.
evidence: This is an inference based on the high P1 value during PTP.

claim: P2 reflects the number of SVs that have moved from the distal (replacement) site to the proximal (docking) site during the time interval separating the first and the second AP (10 ms).
source: P2 then reflects the number of SVs that have moved from the distal (replacement) site to the proximal (docking) site during the time interval separating the first and the second AP (10 ms).
evidence: This is an interpretation of what P2 represents in the context of the RS/DS model.

claim: The transition from replacement site to docking site is likely to occur within a few milliseconds after a strong calcium entry.
source: As this transition is known to occur within a few milliseconds after a strong calcium entry (Miki et al., 2018; Miki et al., 2016), r is likely elevated (possibly close to 1) during the 10-ms interval separating the first two APs.
evidence: This is based on previous studies cited in the text.

claim: As the experimental value of P2 in PTP is 0.67, both ρ (replacement site occupancy) and r (transition probability) are ≥0.67.
source: As the experimental value of P2 in PTP is 0.67, by the same reasoning as above, it follows that both ρ and r are ≥0.67.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the measured P2 value and the model.

claim: The steady-state response at the end of a train is low, indicating that the probability of entry into the replacement site, s, is low.
source: Consistent with this assumption, the steady-state response at the end of a train is low, indicating that the probability of entry into the replacement site, s, is low.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: In 4-AP and after PTP, the sum P1 + P2 can serve as an estimate of the maximal RRP size per docking site.
source: Altogether, our results show that in 4-AP and after PTP, the sum P1 + P2 can serve as an estimate of the maximal RRP size per docking site.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of the experimental conditions and results.

claim: The sum P1 + P2 was significantly larger than 1 both in 4-AP (1.34 ± 0.05; pt < 0.01; n = 14) and during PTP (1.54 ± 0.05; pt < 0.01; n = 8).
source: As shown in the right plot of Figure 4, the sum P1 + P2 was significantly larger than 1 both in 4-AP (1.34 ± 0.05; pt < 0.01; n = 14) and during PTP (1.54 ± 0.05; pt < 0.01; n = 8).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The initial RRP size was larger than 1 SV per docking site both in 4-AP and during PTP.
source: This indicates that the initial RRP size was larger than 1 SV per docking site in both of these experimental conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the P1 + P2 values being significantly greater than 1.

claim: Peak release rates decreased as a function of stimulus number at the end of AP trains in control conditions, reflecting synaptic depression.
source: When examining the time course of release in our control conditions (3 mM Ca0), we found that peak release rates decreased as a function of stimulus number at the end of AP trains, reflecting synaptic depression (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The extent of synaptic depression grew markedly in the presence of 4-AP compared to control.
source: The extent of this depression grew markedly in the presence of 4-AP (second row) compared to control (first row).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental results shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Synaptic depression became even more prominent after PTP.
source: Depression became even more prominent after PTP (third row).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: After inducing PTP in the presence of 4-AP and changing the frequency of stimulation to 200 Hz, synaptic depression was further enhanced to such an extent that individual peak release responses could not be distinguished at the end of the train.
source: In several experiments, after inducing PTP in the presence of 4-AP, we changed the frequency of stimulation to 200 Hz (n = 5). Under these conditions, synaptic depression was further enhanced to such an extent that individual peak release responses could not be distinguished at the end of the train (fourth row).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: While synchronous release is largely due to the fusion of docked SVs upon AP arrival, asynchronous release primarily originates from SVs that did not belong to the RRP at the time of the AP.
source: Previous work suggests that while synchronous release (calculated over a period of 5 ms following each AP: dashed traces in Figure 5B) is largely due to the fusion of docked SVs upon AP arrival, asynchronous release (yellow traces in Figure 5A, B) primarily originates from SVs that did not belong to the RRP at the time of the AP (Miki et al., 2018; Miki et al., 2016; Sakaba, 2006; Tran et al., 2022).
evidence: This is based on previous work cited in the text.

claim: The proportion of asynchronous release gives an indication on the degree of filling of the RRP.
source: Therefore, the proportion of asynchronous release gives an indication on the degree of filling of the RRP.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the origin of asynchronous release.

claim: In control, only synchronous release was observed at the beginning of AP trains, but a significant share of asynchronous release was observed near the end of the train.
source: In control, only synchronous release was observed at the beginning of AP trains, but a significant share of asynchronous release was observed near the end of the train (top panel of Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In 4-AP and during PTP, the proportion of asynchronous release was initially as low as in control, but this proportion increased more rapidly as a function of stimulus number.
source: In 4-AP and during PTP, the proportion of asynchronous release was initially as low as in control, but this proportion increased more rapidly as a function of stimulus number (second and third panels of Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: When increasing the stimulation frequency to 200 Hz during PTP, most release events near the end of the trains were asynchronous, and synchronous release was not detectable for i > 5.
source: Strikingly, when increasing the stimulation frequency to 200 Hz during PTP, most release events near the end of the trains were asynchronous, and synchronous release was not detectable for i > 5 (bottom right panel in Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: RRP depletion during trains increases markedly from one condition to the next and becomes close to complete for 200 Hz stimulation during PTP.
source: Altogether, the evolution of the synchronous component of release during trains (Figure 5A) and that of the proportion of synchronous vs. asynchronous release (Figure 5B) both indicate that RRP depletion during trains increases markedly from one condition to the next and becomes close to complete for 200 Hz stimulation during PTP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: In the 200 Hz condition, s2 is only slightly smaller than s1, and si falls off abruptly as a function of i for i > 2.
source: Here, s2 is only slightly smaller than s1, and si falls off abruptly as a function of i for i > 2.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 5B, bottom right panel.

claim: The fall-off of si for i > 2 in the 200 Hz condition can be fitted by an exponential function with an asymptote at 0 ordinate value, and a time constant of 1.66 inter-AP intervals (corresponding to 8.3 ms).
source: This fall-off can be fitted by an exponential function with an asymptote at 0 ordinate value, and a time constant of 1.66 inter-AP intervals (corresponding to 8.3 ms).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Synaptic depression is weak for i = 2, but very rapid and complete thereafter in the 200 Hz condition.
source: These data indicate that synaptic depression is weak for i = 2, but very rapid and complete thereafter, thus approaching the predictions of the scheme of Figure 1B.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data in relation to the model predictions.

claim: The ratio s8/s1 steeply decreased from 0.83 in control conditions to 0.23, 0.14, and 0.10 in 4-AP, PTP, and 200 Hz, respectively.
source: The resulting curve steeply decreased from 0.83 in control conditions to 0.23, 0.14, and 0.10 in 4-AP, PTP, and 200 Hz, respectively (red curve in Figure 5D, bottom).
evidence: This is a quantitative result shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The paired-pulse ratio (s2/s1) changed much less steeply across experimental conditions, and it remained close to 1 even when s8/s1 had reached very low values.
source: In contrast, the paired-pulse ratio, calculated as s2/s1, changed much less steeply across experimental conditions, and it remained close to 1 even when s8/s1 had reached very low values (green curve in Figure 5D, bottom).
evidence: This is a quantitative result shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The second response in a train is largely immune to synaptic depression, as predicted by the scheme in Figure 1B.
source: This indicates that the second response in a train is largely immune to synaptic depression, as predicted by the scheme in Figure 1B.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the paired-pulse ratio results in relation to model predictions.

claim: The SMN method is accurate only under conditions where the synapse is strongly depressing.
source: The SMN method is accurate only under conditions where the synapse is strongly depressing (Neher, 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about the validity conditions of the SMN method with citation.

claim: The estimated RRP was 0.85 SV per docking site in control, 1.66 SVs per docking site in 4-AP, and 1.87 SVs per docking site in PTP using the SMN method.
source: The estimated RRP was 0.85 SV per docking site in control, 1.66 SVs per docking site in 4-AP, and 1.87 SVs per docking site in PTP.
evidence: These are quantitative results from applying the SMN method, shown in Figure 5B.
